description: Trigger evaluation set for the editorial skill: requests that SHOULD activate it (writing, editing, formatting prose, even when the word editorial is not said) and near-miss negatives that should NOT. Used by the develop trigger smoke test and by `develop optimize`.
should_trigger: draft a reply declining this partnership, keep it warm
write a thank-you email to my landlord
clean up these notes into a doc
proofread this before I send it
turn this rough outline into an essay
reword this message so it sounds less harsh
write the body of this docs page
rewrite the CONTRIBUTING guide so a newcomer can follow it
should_not_trigger: research the current state of solid-state batteries
refactor this function to use async await
build me a skill that drafts invoices
regenerate the API reference from the docstrings
update the agent spec for the QA Engineer
diagram the OAuth login flow for me
what is the capital of Australia
look into whether GLP-1 drugs reduce cardiovascular risk
fix the bug in my Python script
notes: Editorial is structurally scoped: it fires on producing or improving prose a person will read (emails, messages, docs, notes, article bodies), even when the word editorial is absent. It does NOT fire on investigating facts (research), building skills (develop), a chat-only visual (visualize), arithmetic or established-fact lookups, code tasks, or running a repository's scripts and checks. 'Diagram this for me' as a chat answer is visualize; a diagram inside a file under edit would be editorial. Auto-fire also excludes code, generated or machine-written files (logs, build output, any write a script or tool makes), templates, and agent and skill specs, in any repository, even though those are technically text; the repository's own style rules govern the prose it does fire on.
